rounds.text: Amrapali Fincap Ltd trades at an excessive valuation with a trailing P/E ratio between 55.2x and 59.76x, which heavily outpaces the sector benchmark of 26.55x [E1, E6]. This rich multiple is completely disconnected from the company's negligible profitability, demonstrated by a dismal 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year median ROE of 0%, alongside a current ROE of just 0.5% [E13, E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, the business suffers from catastrophic long-term and short-term top-line contraction, registering compounded sales growth of 0% over 10 years, -26% over 5 years, -45% over 3 years, and -29% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16, E17]. This severe deterioration in sales prompted official filings to explicitly flag the company's poor sales growth and low return on equity [E49, E50]. Compounding these fundamental issues for shareholders, the stock currently offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at 0.29x to 0.31x against a sector benchmark of 1.54x, and the stock is trading at the very top of its 52-week range [E2, E5, E7].
